name: lazarus-anti-generic

# Lazarus Anti-Generic

Read repo root `AGENTS.md`, `DESIGN.md`, `docs/WORKFLOW.md`, `docs/TYPOGRAPHY_SYSTEM.md`, `docs/TYPOGRAPHY_QA.md` and `docs/ANTI_GENERIC_AUDIT.md`. Invoke `lazarus-type-director` when available.

## Before coding
1. List verified client-specific facts and intended audience.
2. Write a concrete identity thesis.
3. Explore **seven structurally distinct concept proposals**: each differs in content order, narrative, composition, type treatment, image strategy, and interaction. These are seven original proposals from the client brief, **not seven coded sites** and **not seven one-to-one atlas replicas**. Changing palette alone is not divergence.
4. Compare and choose one; record **all six rejected directions** and their tradeoffs (seven total, not the former three-concept rule).
5. For each of the seven directions, establish a distinct **reading and typographic grammar**, not seven font choices. For the selected direction, compare three monochrome, same-copy type specimens and fill `TYPE_SPEC.md` before code.
6. Name at least two commonly recurring AI defaults that this project intentionally avoids **and why**; don't ban them universally.

## During implementation
Build for real content, responsive interaction, clear focus states, screen-reader-friendly semantics and reduced motion. Avoid filler work, meaningless animations and copied visual compositions. Implement every visible CTA.

## Review
Run the separate typography gate: font licensing, longest true text, 320px/200% resize/reflow, contrast, text spacing overrides, language, font failure and active/focus states. Inspect actual rendering and use Identity Swap, Structural Skeleton, Rationale and Blind Perception tests. Cite observed evidence. Document what was tested and where. A website looking “Apple-like” is not a shortcut to quality.
